newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power slip amid moderate weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power slip amid moderate weather.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the western U.S. continued to slide amid moderate temperatures and abundant supplies, trade sources said Tuesday.
"There are no loads," said one Arizona utility trader.
Traders in the Northwest continued to emphasize the regional abundance of low-cost hydropower as bearish for power prices.
In addition, the spate of power plant outages which emerged last week proved to be short-lived, with most units down only two or three days.
The coming refueling outage of the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant near Wintersburg, Ariz., was expected to help tighten the Southwest market.
"A lot of people are doing balance-of-the-month deals," noted the Arizona trader.
The Palo Verde unit is expected to completely shut Feb 22 for around 50 days.

Meanwhle, the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California was expected to restart sometime during the last week of February after being shut for maintenance and refueling on November 30.
The Pacific Northwest was expected to see average temperatures through Thursday, followed by slightly above normal levels for the weekend.
The Southwest was expected to see below normal temperatures Wednesday, but temperatures were expected to become normal to slightly above by Friday and Saturdaay.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Wednesday was quoted at $10.00-$11.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $10.50-12.00 for Tuesday.
Firm, off-peak COB deliveries for Wednesday were also down slightly at $6.50-7.50.
Firm, peak electricity at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) for Wednesday was quoted at $9.00-10.00, compared with $10.00-11.00 for Tuesday.
Off-peak Mid-C for day-ahead delivery was quoted at $5.50-6.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was quoted at $12.50-13.25, compared with $13.00-14.00 for Tuesday.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $13.00-13.50, while off-peak remained at $7.00-8.00.
